scope: Independent technical-source audit of the C# claims in frozen B07v2. This is not whole-object semantic acceptance, cross-unit review, producer validation, or runtime acceptance.

references.supports: Built-in variance for IEnumerable<T>, IReadOnlyList<T>, IComparer<T>, IComparable<T>; reference-type-only variance conversions; classes such as List<T> remain invariant.
The in/out declaration rules and variance-safe input/output positions for custom generic interfaces.
Delegate variance, including contravariant callback inputs.
Interface, struct, notnull, and public-parameterless-constructor generic constraints and the operations they permit.
Language-specification variance safety and the restriction of variant type parameters to interfaces and delegates.

items.finding: The getter-only interface uses TRevision only as output; reference-type widening to the base revision interface is supported. The class-variance and cast distractors are accurately rejected.
Read and Replace use T in output and input positions, respectively, so neither variance direction is safe for this single mutable interface. The feedback matches the actual option meanings.
IComparer<T> is contravariant; a comparer that accepts TransitEvent can safely consume PlatformChange values. The diagnostics correctly distinguish the int result from T's input positions.

The displayed signature says `TInput Convert(TInput value)`, but the stem then says TOutput is the return type and the keyed in/out answer and Details rely on that. As written, TOutput has no position in the shown method and the return is TInput, so the stem contradicts its own signature.
items.smallestCorrection: Change the displayed signature to `TOutput Convert(TInput value)` and retain the described inheritance relations; then independently verify the option text still expresses input contravariance and output covariance.

items.finding: The covariant conversion is through IEnumerable<T>; List<T> itself remains invariant, and the read-only call-site premise supports the view. Copying is technically possible but is not the variance relationship asked for.

An interface constraint makes StartTime available to the generic body, while the prompt explicitly permits multiple implementations. The feedback accurately rejects runtime casting/reflection as weaker than the stated checked contract.
The struct constraint makes T a non-nullable value type and supports nullable T as an optional value. The distractors do not state equivalent constraints.

The notnull constraint expresses the stated generic type-argument nullability contract without narrowing callers to Character or requiring construction. It is a compile-time nullable-analysis constraint: violations produce warnings rather than runtime enforcement. The candidate does not claim runtime enforcement.
The public parameterless constructor constraint is the language contract required by new T(); the alternative class and notnull constraints do not imply that constructor.
The interface bound justifies the stated generic member accesses and is accurately distinguished from constructor, enum, and runtime-cast approaches.

The prompt guarantees IComparable<T>, but does not require compile-time-only comparison or state that accepted types may lack non-generic IComparable. The keyed bound is the minimal typed contract, but `dynamic` can also invoke CompareTo at runtime, and the non-generic bound can work for types implementing both; the stem does not establish those alternatives as invalid for the stated accepted set.
items.smallestCorrection: State that the generic ranking API must call CompareTo through a compile-time checked contract and that supported entries are not required to implement non-generic IComparable (or replace the alternatives with ones that contradict an explicit premise). Keep the prevalidated non-empty premise.

items.finding: An output-only interface may declare covariance without a class constraint; conversions between constructed variant interfaces are available for reference-type arguments, not value-type arguments.
IReadOnlyList<T> is covariant and List<T> is invariant. The live-view and no-snapshot premises make the keyed interface view distinguishable from the copy alternative.
Action<T> consumes its argument contravariantly, so a handler for the base event can handle the derived event. The option and feedback accurately identify input direction.
The property exposes T in both output and input positions; a mutable generic class cannot declare variance. The option diagnoses align with the actual positions.
An interface constraint permits the generic body to call Format across unrelated implementing classes; the concrete Invoice bound would exclude the stated CreditNote caller.
Each type parameter is output-only and the prompt states reference-type hierarchies, so both may be covariant. The diagnostic correctly avoids inferring direction from the word error.
The input TBase and output TSpecific positions support `in` and `out` independently, with the stated subtype relationship. The reversed and uniform-direction alternatives contradict those positions.

limitations: No C# compiler was available in the workspace (`dotnet`, `csc`, and `mcs` were absent), so no compiler probe was run. The findings are based on official Microsoft language and programming-guide references and source inspection.
This review addresses C# language/API claims and local single-answer technical ambiguities only. It does not establish whole-package semantic acceptance or runtime behavior.
